Fixed in the wave-1 integration of model_pipeline_training.py. Three changes, all in train(): (1) the context loop now iterates sorted(context_set_for_training), so hash order no longer decides anything; (2) the two-branch utterance assembly was replaced by ONE loop that uses the cache when it holds a command and GENERATES when it does not -- the old cached branch silently skipped commands absent from the cache, and a context previously visited as an ancestor has a cache holding only context_model.commands(), which excludes the core commands, so those labels vanished and the commands became unroutable in that context; (3) reserved-label rows are appended from sorted() sets, so row order into the unstratified train_test_split is stable. Note the outcome is now order-INDEPENDENT, not merely order-stable, which is the stronger property.

R3a delivered. Synthetic utterance generation now retries with backoff on RateLimitError and falls back to the command's seed utterances instead of returning [], so a rate-limited command can no longer end a training run silently unroutable. The fallback is recorded in provenance (fell_back / fallback_reason) rather than only logged, which is what makes it visible to the R3b report (fix-551.4) instead of scrolling past in training output.

R4 delivered and integrated. Artifacts are written under ___command_info/versions/<id>/ with a current pointer and per-context compatibility entries, so existing readers resolve unchanged. train_workflow migrates any pre-versioning artifacts into a version BEFORE writing, so a run cannot merge new work into an unrollbackable set; publishes ONLY on success, so a failed train leaves the previous version published and complete with its partial version beside it rather than on top of it; and stamps the manifest with the seed. Provenance is written both top-level (a stable path for the R3b report) and into the version, so a version can still say which personas and seed produced its utterances after a later run overwrites the top-level copy. _prune_stale_artifacts now calls unroute_context instead of shutil.rmtree for compatibility entries -- rmtree refuses to follow a symlink, so without this the prune would have silently stopped cleaning orphans. CLI: fastworkflow versions list|show|publish|prune, and train --version-notes.

Two thresholds with different standing, both labelled as such in the output: the row floor of 4 is DERIVED (the unstratified 25% split gives ~0.25^n odds a command contributes nothing to training; 4 is the smallest n under 1%) and is not an accuracy claim; the seed floor of 8 is ONE workflow's observed curve and is advisory only. ChannelSessionManager gained refcounted per-channel eviction leases: leased_session() takes the lease under the same manager lock that hands out the runtime (invariant 19), initialization_lease() covers creation before the session exists (invariant 20), and _has_work_in_flight() is the union of the registry pointer and a held runtime.lock (invariant 6). Step 7 landed. /invoke_agent_stream is now admitted through the turn registry like every other endpoint: the handler takes an eviction lease, registers a TurnExecution, and returns a StreamingResponse whose body only drains an event queue. Ownership is separated from delivery - a client that disconnects stops reading while the turn keeps the registry pointer and runtime.lock until the work exits. Busy channels now get 409 instead of 200-with-an-error-event (approved wire change); shutdown gets 503. run_owned_turn() in turns.py gives async work the same lifecycle contract as _run_turn. The 504 defect is fixed: run_process_message_with_trace_stream no longer abandons the executor future at its deadline - it reports the timeout to the client via on_timeout and still awaits the future, so no detached thread can mutate a context that eviction or shutdown has closed. Shutdown quiescence per section 10.5: admission is closed atomically via TurnRegistry.close_admission() before draining, the drain uses the union predicate plus leases (busy_channel_ids) instead of runtime.lock.locked(), and after the deadline still-busy runtimes are NEVER finalized or closed - logged at ERROR and left to the host. 5 new integration tests in tests/test_fastapi_streaming_lifecycle.py.

Step 8 landed. New fastworkflow/state_serialization.py is the single strict serializer: validate_state / encode_state / state_digest. It requires a dict at the top level, string keys recursively, JSON-native values only, and rejects NaN and infinities, cycles, and identity-significant sharing (the same mutable container reachable by two paths, which would restore as independent copies). Errors name the path to the offending value so an author can act on them. Canonical encoding is sorted keys, compact separators, allow_nan=False, so equal states produce identical digests and retirement does not write on every turn. The default=str round-trip is removed from WorkflowExecutionContext.serialize_state - the FIRST serializer, which is what made every downstream strictness check vacuous - and from both DiskSessionStateStore.save and RedisSessionStateStore.save. Invariant 8 is honoured at both persist call sites: an encoding failure logs a warning and skips the write, leaving the runtime live with its state in memory, rather than writing something restore would trust. 12 new tests in tests/test_state_serialization.py, five of them driven THROUGH ctx.serialize_state() as section 11.4 requires, since testing the encoder in isolation is how the previous revision's strictness requirement passed review while being unimplementable. Note: filtering to declared-durable keys (section 11.4 item 2) arrives with the hook mechanism in fix-g03.17.

Checkpoint namespace lifecycle implemented in fastworkflow/checkpoint_store.py (206 tests, 15/15 mutations killed). RetentionPolicy states the policy rather than hiding a TTL (decision 16): an age window plus max_channels/max_bytes caps, with describe() printing the resulting byte ceiling because a count cap is unauditable without it. The reaper is INVOKED, never scheduled - no thread inside the store, since a background sweeper would be a second writer per channel (invariant 15); the server drives it from a lifespan task every 300s and names every live or leased channel as protected. Crash safety is publish's prepare-then-flip run backwards: reclamation makes a complete channel invisible with one rename, so no interrupted pass leaves a readable partial generation, and debris sweeping runs first. Operator API: inspect/list_channels, quarantine/list_quarantine_entries, delete, reset, reap(dry_run=), stats(). Channel reuse is safe two ways - delete is one atomic rename so nothing of the old lineage survives to adopt, and reset records a generation floor so numbers never repeat. stats().total_bytes_physical is what the section 16.5 plateau gate measures. Stated limits: nothing is reclaimed unless reap is called; growth between passes is unbounded; one record's size is unbounded; caps are per namespace; a fingerprint that changes every deploy creates a namespace whose predecessor is reclaimed only by age.

MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS resolver landed with the default lowered 2000 -> 50. resolve_max_live_sessions() reads the PROCESS ENVIRONMENT FIRST, then workflow env files, then the default, and returns the value with its source. OS-first is not a preference: get_env_var returns a supplied default BEFORE consulting os.environ, so passing a default would make the container variable unreachable and the documented default would outrank the operator override. Resolution runs in the lifespan after fastworkflow.init() has loaded the env files, and an unusable value (non-integer, zero, negative) raises at startup rather than rejecting traffic later. The effective value and source are logged on their own line and in the section 17 memory-bounds record. fastworkflow/examples/fastworkflow.env documents the knob as a COMMENTED line with the reason - an active assignment there would shadow the deployment's own value, reintroducing the defect through the file the resolver reads second. Also wired: trimming re-runs after a turn clears its active pointer, once the registry lock is released (section 12, invariant 17), because a channel skipped for being busy becomes retirable the moment its turn ends and nothing else revisits it. 12 tests in tests/test_max_live_sessions_resolver.py, including one asserting the env template never assigns the variable.

Fixed by making the fingerprint source-dependent, but resolved from the source's CLASS rather than its instance state.

The issue framed source-dependence as 'a different shape from the current design'. On inspection that does not hold: the persona_source fingerprint input was ALREADY a function of the installed source, because active_persona_source_label() consults the process-wide source and returns name#fingerprint(). Only a third component was added: name#<content fingerprint>#<pool-code digest>.

The digest comes from PersonaSource.pool_source_digest(), which hashes the source text of every function the concrete class and its bases define, found BY REFLECTION. Reflection rather than a name list is the whole point -- a name list is exactly what left _matches and rows out in the first place: fix-k0i.43 named four functions, two more existed, and nothing failed. Adding DomainConditionedPersonaSource._matches to _DIGESTED_GENERATION_SOURCES was rejected for that reason, and because it would make EVERY workflow regenerate over a keyword filter only a workflow with personas.json can reach.

Determinism verified independently rather than argued: the digest is identical across PYTHONHASHSEED 0/12345/99999 in fresh subprocesses, and is computable from an uninitialised instance -- confirming it reads only type(self), so no instance attribute and no id() can reach it. Ordered by MRO then attribute name so neither __dict__ order nor the hash salt can move it. Properties are unwrapped to .fget and staticmethod/classmethod to .__func__, because inspect.getsource rejects the descriptors and source_digest would otherwise have quietly recorded 'source-unavailable' -- a digest that stops noticing edits while still looking like one.
